newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela reaches preliminary accord with unions.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela reaches preliminary accord with unions.

text.p: After nearly two months of strikes and strident public debate, the Venezuelan government has reached a preliminary accord with public sector workers over pay rises for the coming year, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said.
The wage hike "is above the expected (25 percent) inflation rate for 1997," Matos told reporters in Congress, but did not give more precise details.
Late last week, however, Labor Minister Juan Nepomuceno Garrido had said the government was considering a 30 percent across-the-board rise.
The agreement, signed this morning with Venezuela's largest public sector union, the Confederation of Venezuelan Workers (CTV), still has to be cleared with other Venezuelan unions, Matos added.

While the proposal tops an earlier 25 percent offer, Matos said: "No one can expect this government to put right in one stroke the problem of Venezuela's low real wages, which has accumulated over the past 15 years."
Venezuelan real wages, laid waste by triple-digit inflation last year, have shrunk to some 30 percent of 1980 levels, according to government estimates.
In January, the government awarded an average 164 percent pay rise to striking doctors, fanning other wage demands.

Some 40,000 university teachers are currently on strike over a 125 percent pay claim. The work action grew heated last Wednesday as police fired tear gas and plastic bullets to break up a banned student protest over low teachers' pay and insufficient university funding.
